from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "PCR setup", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # load labware
    tips = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 2)
    src_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 3)
    dst_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 4)

    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips])

    # define master mix liquid
    mm = protocol.define_liquid(name="master mix", description="PCR master mix", display_color="#FF0000")
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=mm, volume=2000)  # enough for 96*18=1728 ul

    # define template liquids (one per well)
    for col in range(1, 13):
        col_str = f"{col}"
        for row in "ABCDEFGH":
            well_name = f"{row}{col_str}"
            liq_name = f"template_{well_name}"
            liq = protocol.define_liquid(name=liq_name, description=f"Template {well_name}", display_color="#00FF00")
            src_plate[well_name].load_liquid(liquid=liq, volume=50)  # reasonable starting volume

    # distribute master mix using single tip (re-use)
    tip_wells = tips.wells()
    tip_idx = 0
    def get_tip():
        nonlocal tip_idx
        if tip_idx >= len(tip_wells):
            raise RuntimeError("Out of tips")
        tip = tip_wells[tip_idx]
        tip_idx += 1
        return tip

    p300.pick_up_tip(get_tip())
    wells_done = 0
    while wells_done < 96:
        # how many wells we can fill with current tip volume
        max_aspirate = p300.tip_rack.max_volume  # 300 ul
        batch = min(max_aspirate // 18, 96 - wells_done)
        vol_needed = batch * 18
        p300.aspirate(vol_needed, reservoir["A1"])
        for i in range(batch):
            dst_well = dst_plate.wells()[wells_done + i]
            p300.dispense(18, dst_well)
        p300.blow_out(reservoir["A1"])
        wells_done += batch
    p300.drop_tip()

    # add templates, fresh tip each well
    for col in range(1, 13):
        col_str = f"{col}"
        for row in "ABCDEFGH":
            src_well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            dst_well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(2, src_plate[src_well])
            p300.dispense(2, dst_plate[dst_well])
            p300.drop_tip()
"}

{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "PCR setup", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # labware
    tips1 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    tips2 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 4)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 2)
    src_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 3)
    dst_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 5)

    # instruments
    p300_single = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips1, tips2])
    p20_single = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "left", tip_racks=[tips1, tips2])

    # liquids
    mm = protocol.define_liquid(name="master mix", description="PCR master mix", display_color="#FF0000")
    water = protocol.define_liquid(name="water", description="NTC water", display_color="#0000FF")
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=mm, volume=2000)          # master mix
    reservoir["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=water, volume=100)       # water for NTC

    # template liquids (one per well)
    for col in range(1, 13):
        col_str = f"{col}"
        for row in "ABCDEFGH":
            well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            liq_name = f"template_{well}"
            liq = protocol.define_liquid(name=liq_name, description=f"Template {well}", display_color="#00FF00")
            src_plate[well].load_liquid(liquid=liq, volume=50)

    # ---- master mix distribution (single channel, reuse tip) ----
    p300_single.pick_up_tip()
    wells_done = 0
    while wells_done < 96:
        batch = min(300 // 18, 96 - wells_done)  # 16 wells per aspiration
        vol = batch * 18
        p300_single.aspirate(vol, reservoir["A1"])
        for i in range(batch):
            dst_well = dst_plate.wells()[wells_done + i]
            p300_single.dispense(18, dst_well)
        p300_single.blow_out(reservoir["A1"])
        wells_done += batch
    p300_single.drop_tip()

    # ---- template addition (p20, fresh tip each well) ----
    for col in range(1, 13):
        col_str = f"{col}"
        for row in "ABCDEFGH":
            src_well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            dst_well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            p20_single.pick_up_tip()
            p20_single.aspirate(2, src_plate[src_well])
            p20_single.dispense(2, dst_plate[dst_well])
            p20_single.mix_after=(5, 16)  # mix after dispensing
            p20_single.drop_tip()

    # ---- add NTC well (H12) with water instead of template ----
    p20_single.pick_up_tip()
    p20_single.aspirate(2, reservoir["A2"])   # water
    p20_single.dispense(2, dst_plate["H12"])
    p20_single.mix_after=(5, 16)
    p20_single.drop_tip()
"}

protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 2 notes).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A2 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 60:  p20_single.aspirate(2, reservoir["A2"])   # water
   At line 60 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from water (well A2 in slot 2) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 100 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.55 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air.
   The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from
   these draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 2.
   Also reached 1 other well: well H12 in slot 5.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [fd004ea641d2]

2. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 96 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 41:  p300_single.dispense(18, dst_well)
   At line 41 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 5), and 96 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 88 more in slot 5.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 5.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 18 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [fb75767309e4]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 96 wells never mixed after template_A1, template_B1, template_C1,
template_D1 and 92 more went in (10% of the well)
   line 54:  p20_single.dispense(2, dst_plate[dst_well])
   At line 54 the robot added template_A1, template_B1, template_C1, template_D1 and 92 more
   to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 5, which already held master
   mix (this line did it 96 times). The addition was 10% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 5.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 5 after line 54:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [61b3ca310923]

{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "PCR setup", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # labware
    tips1 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    tips2 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 4)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 2)
    src_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 3)
    dst_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 5)

    # instruments
    p300_single = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips1, tips2])
    p20_single = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "left", tip_racks=[tips1, tips2])

    # liquids
    mm = protocol.define_liquid(name="master mix", description="PCR master mix", display_color="#FF0000")
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=mm, volume=2000)          # master mix

    # Define water liquid that will serve as NTC but named as template_H12
    water_ntc = protocol.define_liquid(name="template_H12", description="NTC water", display_color="#0000FF")
    # We'll need a source of water; use reservoir A2
    water_source = protocol.define_liquid(name="water_source", description="Water reservoir", display_color="#0000FF")
    reservoir["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=water_source, volume=500)

    # Define template liquids for all wells except H12
    for col in range(1, 13):
        col_str = f"{col}"
        for row in "ABCDEFGH":
            well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            if row == "H" and col_str == "12":
                # H12 will get the water_ntc liquid (already defined)
                continue
            liq_name = f"template_{well}"
            liq = protocol.define_liquid(name=liq_name, description=f"Template {well}", display_color="#00FF00")
            src_plate[well].load_liquid(liquid=liq, volume=50)

    # Load the NTC water into source well H12
    src_plate["H12"].load_liquid(liquid=water_ntc, volume=50)

    # ---- master mix distribution (single channel, reuse tip) ----
    p300_single.pick_up_tip()
    wells_done = 0
    while wells_done < 96:
        batch = min(300 // 18, 96 - wells_done)  # 16 wells per aspiration
        vol = batch * 18
        p300_single.aspirate(vol, reservoir["A1"])
        for i in range(batch):
            dst_well = dst_plate.wells()[wells_done + i]
            p300_single.dispense(18, dst_well)
        p300_single.blow_out(reservoir["A1"])
        wells_done += batch
    p300_single.drop_tip()

    # ---- template addition (p20, fresh tip each well) ----
    for col in range(1, 13):
        col_str = f"{col}"
        for row in "ABCDEFGH":
            src_well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            dst_well = f"{row}{col_str}"
            p20_single.pick_up_tip()
            p20_single.aspirate(2, src_plate[src_well])
            p20_single.dispense(2, dst_plate[dst_well])
            p20_single.mix(repetitions=5, volume=16, location=dst_plate[dst_well])
            p20_single.drop_tip()
"}
